Meeting Minutes 2 - Project Branding and Proposal Planning

Author

Haley

Published

June 7, 2026

Meeting Information

Item Details
Date 7 June 2026
Time 15:30 – 18:00
Venue LKSLIB
Present All members (Helen, Haley, Edith)
Absent Nil

Opening

The meeting was called to order at 15:30 by all members at LKSLIB. All three members were present. The agenda was reviewed and approved.

Meeting objectives included: - Finalising the project name and branding direction - Discussing the logo design and slogan - Planning the proposal structure and content - Planning the next steps, professor consultation, and assignment submission strategy

Approval of Minutes

Minutes of Meeting 1 (27 May 2026) were reviewed and approved by all members.

Business from Previous Meeting

The team noted that task allocations from Meeting 1 remain pending. Members confirmed they are actively working on their respective components (data processing, website, meeting minutes and Question 2).

Discussion on Project Name Change

The team agreed that the previously considered name “Punchnet” carried connotations that were too strong and not fully aligned with the project’s analytical and investigative nature.

Helen said: “I think ‘Punchnet’ sounds a bit too aggressive and doesn’t really capture the forensic storytelling we want. We need something that reflects tracing and discovery.”

Edith said: “Agreed. What about ‘EchoTrace’? It suggests following digital echoes to find anomalies – that’s exactly what our Shiny app will do.”

Haley said: “I like that. It’s memorable and fits the cybersecurity angle without being overly technical.”

Conclusion: The team unanimously agreed to rename the project to “EchoTrace”.

Discussion on Logo Design Direction

The team discussed visual elements for the new EchoTrace logo.

Edith said: “I can take responsibility for the logo. I’m thinking of an eye‑detection motif – something like a stylised eye or a magnifying glass, Sherlock Holmes style.”

Haley said: “That’s perfect. It ties into investigation and anomaly detection.”

Helen said: “What about colours? We should use a dynamic, high‑contrast gradient – maybe a fighter print gradient.”

Edith said: “Yes, that will make the logo stand out on both the website and the Shiny interface.”

Conclusion: - Logo responsibility: Edith - Motif: Eye‑detection / investigative (magnifying glass or stylised eye) - Colour scheme: Fighter print gradient colour (dynamic, high‑contrast gradient)

Discussion on Project Slogan

The team moved to finalising a slogan that would accompany the EchoTrace branding.

Haley said: “We need something short, punchy, and meaningful. How about ‘Trace the echo. Find the anomaly.’?”

Helen said: “I really like that. It captures both the forensic tracing and the detection purpose.”

Edith said: “Agreed. It’s easy to remember and fits perfectly on the website header.”

Conclusion: The team adopted the slogan: “Trace the echo. Find the anomaly.” It will be used on the project website and within the Shiny application interface.

Discussion on Proposal Structure and Content

The team discussed what the project proposal should include to ensure alignment with the professor’s expectations and the project’s analytical goals.

Haley said: “We need a clear problem statement summarising Mini Challenge 2 – the cybersecurity anomaly detection challenge. We should list our six analytical stories: sequence reconstruction, message generation chain, system architecture, provenance analysis, historical pattern detection, and intervention simulation. We also need a technical approach section – Shiny architecture, data processing pipeline, visualisation libraries like plotly and visNetwork.”

Haley said: “The proposal should be concise but detailed enough to show feasibility. Let’s aim for a draft before our professor consultation.”

Conclusion: The team agreed on the following proposal outline:

# Proposal Section
1 Project title and branding (EchoTrace, slogan, logo direction)
2 Problem statement – summarising Mini Challenge 2
3 Proposed analytical stories (six core narratives)
4 Technical approach – Shiny architecture, data pipeline, visualisation libraries
5 Key features and user interaction design
6 Work distribution and timeline (building on Meeting 1 allocations)
7 Risk assessment and mitigation strategies

The target is to complete a draft proposal before the next professor consultation.

Discussion on Next Meeting and Professor Consultation

The team planned logistics for the upcoming consultation with the professor.

Edith said: “We should meet before the consultation to prepare our questions and a draft proposal.”

Helen said: “Let’s do a Zoom meeting tomorrow – Tuesday 8 June.”

Helen said: “What time? Evening works best for me.”

Conclusion: The team agreed on the following:

  • Next meeting: Tuesday 8 June 2026 via Zoom
  • Time: 19:00
  • Purpose: To prepare for and conduct a consultation session with the professor

Discussion on Assignment Submission and Intellectual Property Protection

The team discussed SMU academic integrity rules regarding the sharing of assignment materials before deadlines.

Haley said: “We should not share any part of our assignment until after the take‑home assignment 2 deadline passes as it might violate SMU interity rule”

Edith said: “Absolutely. That protects our unique ideas and prevents accidental violations.”

Haley said: “It also ensures we build a strong, unified project based on our own original work.”

Conclusion: It was unanimously agreed that the team will not share any assignment components with other parties until after the deadline. This approach protects intellectual property and maintains academic integrity.

Additions to the Agenda

No additional items were raised.

Adjournment

The meeting was adjourned at 18:00 by all members.
